statement: With first shape held, every path with diverging second shape and second shape divided by scale converging to a positive rate has the corresponding gamma likelihood limit.
hypotheses_and_conclusion:
{ι : Type*} {l : Filter ι} {x : Fin n → ℝ}
    (hx : ∀ i, 0 < x i) {p r : ℝ} (hp : 0 < p) (hr : 0 < r)
    {q s : ι → ℝ} (hq : Tendsto q l atTop) (hs : ∀ᶠ j in l, 0 < s j)

    Tendsto (fun j ↦ BetaPrime.logLik x (s j) (p, q j)) l
      (𝓝 (∑ i, Gamma.logDensity p r (x i)))
dossier_scope_note: Any joint path with converging positive gamma rate.

statement: With second shape held, the reciprocal path with diverging first shape and first shape times scale tending to a positive rate gives the inverse-gamma likelihood, including the data Jacobian.

      (𝓝 ((∑ i, Gamma.logDensity q r (x i)⁻¹) - ∑ i, 2 * log (x i)))
dossier_scope_note: Any joint path with converging positive inverse-gamma parameter.

statement: At any fixed finite likelihood level for a held first shape, the second shape is bounded below and its ratio to scale lies in a compact positive interval. This holds for every nonempty positive sample.

statement: For a maximizing sequence escaping every compact subset of the positive shape and scale domain at held first shape, the second shape must diverge and its ratio to scale must converge to the fitted gamma rate. Consequently the sequence has exactly the fitted gamma value.

    (hesc : ∀ K : Set (ℝ × ℝ), IsCompact K → K ⊆ Beta.domain →

    (hlim : Tendsto (fun j ↦ BetaPrime.logLik x (s j) (p, q j)) atTop (𝓝 M)) :
    let r := Gamma.rate x p
    Tendsto q atTop atTop ∧ Tendsto (fun j ↦ q j / s j) atTop (𝓝 r) ∧
      M = ∑ i, Gamma.logDensity p r (x i)
dossier_scope_note: Every escaping maximizing sequence converges in scaled rate to the fitted gamma.

statement: At fixed beta shapes every attained endpoint and power fit is unique. Its endpoint is sample contact at unit upper shape and is strictly above the sample at greater upper shape.

statement: When the finite inverse Pareto witness test fails, the fitted inverse exponential value is a strict least upper bound, reached in the limit along the fitted-rate path. This includes constant positive samples.
hypotheses_and_conclusion:
{n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) {x : Fin n → ℝ}
    (hx : ∀ i, 0 < x i)
    (hw : ¬ ∃ u ∈ Ioo 0 (Lomax.uBar (Transfer.reciprocal x)),
      Lomax.psi (Transfer.reciprocal x) u ≤ 0) :
    let L := fun p : ℝ × ℝ ↦ Transfer.InvPareto.logLik x p.1 p.2
    let r := (Lomax.avg (Transfer.reciprocal x))⁻¹
    let C := Transfer.InvPareto.bestInvExp x
    IsLUB (L '' Lomax.domain) C ∧
